Aatrox.build: Aatrox’s main damage is physical, and Jayce has low armor, so start with Cloth Armor to build armor first, then buy Plated Steelcaps. If fights drag on because of Aatrox P Deathbringer Stance, Aatrox E Umbral Dash, and the healing from Aatrox R World Ender, fit in Executioner's Calling.
Aatrox.combo: In cannon form, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. If you have a chance to close in and finish the fight, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, leap in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, then use a basic attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow in that order. Aim the final knockback to push the opponent in the direction you want.
Aatrox.escape: Right after Aatrox uses Aatrox E Umbral Dash is your chance to close the distance. If Aatrox W Infernal Chains catches you, leave its area first, then look for a chance to go in with Jayce Q To the Skies!.
Aatrox.fight: Trade right after Aatrox uses the empowered basic attack from Aatrox P Deathbringer Stance on a minion. Avoid the edge of Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade while poking with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form. When Aatrox R World Ender is active, create distance and wait for its duration to end.
Aatrox.laning: In cannon form, disrupt last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast, but keep the wave near the center. Farm without giving Aatrox an early kill. If he closes in, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer and knock him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Aatrox.phase: Jayce is strongest early, but Aatrox can also snowball quickly if he gains an early lead, so look for lane advantage without giving up a kill. In mid game, turn the lead you have built into objective gains. Jayce is vulnerable if caught in the late game, so fight from a safe distance.
Aatrox.teamfight: Start the team fight from the back line with Jayce Q Shock Blast fired through Jayce E Acceleration Gate. Switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer and briefly go in only when the enemy formation is disrupted; after your combo, switch to cannon and retreat.
Aatrox.watch: Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade deals major damage and knocks you up, so watch its cast and dodge outside the blade’s edge or move close to Aatrox.

Akali.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Akali's main damage is magic and Jayce has low magic resistance, so prioritize building magic resistance. Also build enough health to withstand the second hit of Akali R Perfect Execution.
Akali.combo: When poking, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it immediately. If Akali comes out of the smoke to start a fight, hit her with Jayce Q Shock Blast, then use Jayce R Mercury Hammer, Jayce Q To the Skies!, a basic attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow in that order. Aim the final knockback to push Akali in the direction you want.
Akali.escape: Check whether Akali W Twilight Shroud and E Shuriken Flip have been used before going in. If only one is down, she can escape with the other mobility spell, so don't overextend to chase her. In particular, trade before Akali R Perfect Execution comes back by closing the distance with Jayce Q To the Skies! and knocking her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Akali.fight: If Akali comes out of Akali W Twilight Shroud to attack, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, fight back, and knock her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow. Build a health and CS lead while Akali R Perfect Execution is unavailable.
Akali.laning: Keep the wave near the center and poke with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form to disrupt last hits. If Akali closes in, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer to gain resistances and use Jayce E Thundering Blow to push her away.
Akali.phase: Build a lead through lane advantage and objectives in the early and mid game. In the late game, Jayce is in danger if caught, so don't go deep first.
Akali.teamfight: Start the team fight from the back line with Jayce Q Shock Blast. If Akali closes in with Akali E Shuriken Flip or R Perfect Execution, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer and knock her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow. Go in briefly only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to cannon and retreat.
Akali.watch: If marked, Akali's second dash will follow you even if you try to escape, so knock her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow when she goes in.

Aurora.build: Aurora's damage is mostly magic, and Jayce has relatively low magic resistance, so buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads. Aurora P Spirit Abjuration can heal back your poke damage, so also fit in Executioner's Calling.
Aurora.combo: In cannon form, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it to hit Aurora. If you have an opening to go in, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, then use a basic attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow in that order. Land the basic attack with bonus damage right after switching to hammer, and aim Jayce E Thundering Blow to push Aurora in the direction you want.
Aurora.escape: Don't go straight in just because Aurora W Across the Veil is down. Close the distance with Jayce Q To the Skies! after Aurora E The Weirding is also down and before Aurora R Between Worlds comes back, especially once the danger from Aurora Q Twofold Hex's return has passed. After going in, aim Jayce E Thundering Blow to push Aurora in the direction you want.
Aurora.fight: Poke first with Jayce Q Shock Blast fired through Jayce E Acceleration Gate, keeping the gap between placing the gate and firing short. If Aurora W Across the Veil and E The Weirding have both been used, or before Aurora R Between Worlds comes back, look for a chance to go in with Jayce Q To the Skies!. Avoid trades where you are left low while waiting for Aurora Q Twofold Hex's return damage.
Aurora.laning: Early on, use both of Jayce's forms to poke and disrupt last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form. Keep the wave near the center and don't push it all the way in. If Aurora closes in, switch to hammer to gain armor and magic resistance, then create distance by knocking her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Aurora.phase: In mid game, turn that lead into an objective advantage. In late-game team fights, you're vulnerable if caught, so poke from the back and go in briefly before retreating.
Aurora.teamfight: Start the team fight from the back line with Jayce Q Shock Blast fired through Jayce E Acceleration Gate, and go in briefly with hammer only when the enemy formation is disrupted. If Aurora uses Aurora W Across the Veil, her leap, to engage and doesn't participate in a kill, you have a window to catch her. But if she participates in a kill, its cooldown resets, so don't leave low-health allies behind. After your hammer combo, switch to cannon and retreat, using your next basic attack to reduce Aurora's armor and magic resistance.
Aurora.watch: If Aurora Q Twofold Hex hits you, it deals damage again when the curse returns, so move out of the line between Aurora and yourself. The return damage increases the lower your health is, so don't stay in while cursed. Back off before Aurora R Between Worlds forms. While Aurora W Across the Veil makes her invisible, wait for her to reappear or aim Jayce Q Shock Blast at where she is likely to arrive.

Camille.build: Camille's damage is mostly physical, and Jayce has low armor, so start with Cloth Armor to build armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. If the healing from Camille W Tactical Sweep restores the damage from your poke, fit in Executioner's Calling.
Camille.combo: When poking, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. If Camille E Hookshot is down and you can keep attacking at close range, use this order: land cannon Q → switch with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer to hammer form → Jayce Q To the Skies! → basic attack → Jayce W Lightning Field → Jayce E Thundering Blow. The basic attack right after switching to hammer deals bonus magic damage.
Camille.escape: After Camille E Hookshot is down is your chance to close the distance with Jayce Q To the Skies!. However, if Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum is still available, don't go deep just because E is down; look for an opening when R is also unavailable. If Camille traps you with Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum, don't waste Jayce E Thundering Blow when she casts it; wait out the zone's duration, then counterattack.
Camille.fight: Avoid trading just after Camille P Adaptive Defenses grants her a shield; attack after the shield wears off. Poke first with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form, and go in with Jayce Q To the Skies! when Camille E Hookshot is down. Create distance while waiting for Camille Q Precision Protocol's second empowered basic attack.
Camille.laning: Early on, disrupt Camille's last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form and keep the wave near the center. Camille can only engage if Camille E Hookshot catches a wall, so don't let yourself get pushed toward one. Take lane priority and deny her farm before Camille gets her first core item.
Camille.phase: Jayce is strong early, and Camille clears waves slowly before her first core item, so build a lead in farm and lane priority during that time. From mid game onward, Camille can quickly take side lane towers, so don't leave a side lane unattended. Jayce is vulnerable if caught in late-game team fights, so use the advantage you built early and mid game.
Camille.teamfight: Start the team fight from the back line with Jayce Q Shock Blast, and be ready to interrupt Camille E Hookshot's engage with Jayce E Thundering Blow. Go in briefly to use your hammer combo only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then immediately switch to cannon and retreat.
Camille.watch: Camille E Hookshot lets her dash a long distance along a wall and stun you, so stand away from walls. Save Jayce E Thundering Blow so you can interrupt her leap as soon as her hook catches a wall. Camille Q Precision Protocol's second empowered basic attack deals true damage, so create distance while she prepares that attack.

Chogath.build: Cho'Gath Q Rupture, W Feral Scream, and E Vorpal Spikes deal magic damage, so buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads. If Cho'Gath P Carnivore heals back the damage from your poke, fit in Executioner's Calling. Magic resistance cannot reduce the true damage from Cho'Gath R Feast.
Chogath.combo: In cannon form, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it to hit Cho'Gath. If you can dodge Cho'Gath Q Rupture and go in, attack in this order: Jayce Q Shock Blast → switch to hammer with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer → Jayce Q To the Skies! → basic attack → Jayce W Lightning Field → Jayce E Thundering Blow. Land the basic attack right after switching to hammer, and use the final knockback to push Cho'Gath in the direction you want.
Chogath.escape: The window to go in is right after Cho'Gath uses Q Rupture on the wave or misses it. Cho'Gath has no mobility spell, so close the distance with Jayce Q To the Skies! then, but avoid the front of Cho'Gath W Feral Scream.
Chogath.fight: When you see the warning for Cho'Gath Q Rupture, move sideways, and use the movement speed gained when switching forms with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer to manage distance. Avoid the front of Cho'Gath W Feral Scream while poking in cannon form with Jayce Q Shock Blast fired through Jayce E Acceleration Gate. If Cho'Gath Q Rupture misses and you get a chance to go in, engage with Jayce Q To the Skies! and trade briefly, aiming Jayce E Thundering Blow to push him in the direction you want.
Chogath.laning: Early on, poke from outside his range with Jayce Q Shock Blast and disrupt Cho'Gath's last hits. Cho'Gath E Vorpal Spikes pass through minions and continue behind them, so stand off the line where Cho'Gath is basic attacking. Pressure him while keeping the wave near the center, and look for a gank right after Cho'Gath uses Q Rupture on the wave.
Chogath.phase: Jayce is strong in the early game when he can use both forms, so pressure the lane first. Turn the advantage you gain in the early and mid game into a lead in lane and objectives. Cho'Gath's Feast stacks make the matchup worse over time, so don't give him a kill when your health is low.
Chogath.teamfight: Start the team fight from the back line with Jayce E Acceleration Gate and Jayce Q Shock Blast, and keep your distance while watching the ranges of Cho'Gath Q Rupture and W Feral Scream. Go in briefly with hammer only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to cannon and retreat.
Chogath.watch: Cho'Gath Q Rupture knocks you up after a warning appears beneath you, so immediately dodge sideways when you see the mark. Cho'Gath W Feral Scream silences in front of him, making the Q that follows harder to dodge, so don't start trades from the front. If your health is at or below half, move out of range of Cho'Gath R Feast, which deals true damage.

Darius.build: Darius's main damage is physical, so start with Cloth Armor to build armor first, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. If the healing from Darius Q Decimate restores the damage from your poke, fit in Executioner's Calling. Darius E Apprehend pierces some armor and R Noxian Guillotine deals true damage, so don't rely on armor alone to fight for long.
Darius.combo: When poking, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. If Darius E Apprehend is down and you can go in, fight briefly in this order: cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast → switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer → Jayce Q To the Skies! → basic attack → Jayce W Lightning Field → Jayce E Thundering Blow. Use the final Jayce E Thundering Blow to create distance from Darius.
Darius.escape: When Darius E Apprehend misses or is on cooldown, you have an opening to go in. But if Darius P Hemorrhage stacks build up, knock him away with Jayce E Thundering Blow and retreat.
Darius.fight: Poke briefly from outside Darius E Apprehend's range with Jayce Q Shock Blast fired through Jayce E Acceleration Gate. Trade after Darius E Apprehend misses or right after he uses Q Decimate to clear minions, then knock him away with Jayce E Thundering Blow and end the fight quickly. Stop chasing and create distance as Darius P Hemorrhage stacks start to build.
Darius.laning: In cannon form, stay outside Darius E Apprehend's range and disrupt last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast. Don't push the wave all the way in; keep it near the center and repeat short pokes. In positions where you're at high risk of being grabbed, switch to hammer to gain armor, and knock Darius away with Jayce E Thundering Blow if he closes in.
Darius.phase: In the early and mid game, turn the advantage from short trades into a lead in lane and objectives. In late-game team fights, Jayce is vulnerable if caught, so prioritize staying out of Darius E Apprehend's range.
Darius.teamfight: Start the team fight from the back line with Jayce Q Shock Blast, and go in briefly only when Darius E Apprehend is down or the enemy formation is disrupted. After your hammer combo, switch to cannon and retreat. Don't stay in with Darius P Hemorrhage stacks built up and allow Darius R Noxian Guillotine to secure a kill and reset its cooldown.
Darius.watch: If Darius E Apprehend pulls you in, he can follow with Darius W Crippling Strike and Q Decimate, so poke outside E's range and keep Jayce Q To the Skies! available to respond. When you see Darius Q Decimate, move outside the blade's edge or hug him closely to reduce its damage and healing. If Darius P Hemorrhage stacks build up, create distance to break the stacks; with several stacks, retreat fully outside Darius R Noxian Guillotine's range.

DrMundo.build: Dr. Mundo's main damage is physical, and Jayce has low armor, so start with Cloth Armor to withstand it and choose Plated Steelcaps. Even after building armor, if fights drag on because of the healing from Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases, Q Infected Bonesaw, and W Heart Zapper, fit in Executioner's Calling.
DrMundo.combo: If Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is down, hit him with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form, then switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer. Follow with Jayce Q To the Skies!, a basic attack, W Lightning Field, and E Thundering Blow, aiming E Thundering Blow to push Mundo in the direction you want. As you retreat, switch to Jayce R Mercury Cannon and land one more basic attack to lower Mundo's armor and magic resistance.
DrMundo.escape: Dr. Mundo has no skill that creates distance on his own, so look for an angle to close in with Jayce Q To the Skies! after Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is down. Dodge Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw from behind minions, and look to engage while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is down. After going in, use Jayce E Thundering Blow in the direction that best suits chasing or disengaging.
DrMundo.fight: In cannon form, quickly chain Jayce E Acceleration Gate and Q Shock Blast to poke, and keep trades short to account for Dr. Mundo's healing. If Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases is available, it blocks the knockback from Jayce E Thundering Blow, so look for a close-range engage after his passive is down. The window while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is down is a good time to attempt a kill.
DrMundo.laning: Keep the wave near the center and disrupt Dr. Mundo's last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form. Keep a minion between you to dodge Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw, but account for Jayce Q Shock Blast detonating on the spot if it hits a minion. If you can step on a canister Dr. Mundo dropped while retreating after a trade, do so to deny his healing and passive cooldown reduction.
DrMundo.phase: In mid game, turn that advantage into objective gains and look for openings while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is down. In late-game team fights, Jayce is vulnerable if caught, so keep your engage brief.
DrMundo.teamfight: Start the team fight from the back line with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form, and go in with hammer only when the enemy formation is disrupted. After using your combo on the back line, switch immediately to cannon and retreat. If Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is active, shift your focus to other enemies or objectives instead of spending time trying to kill Mundo.
DrMundo.watch: Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw hits only the first target it hits and deals more damage the higher your current health is, so dodge it with a minion between you. When Dr. Mundo activates R Maximum Dosage, his healing and movement speed increase, so don't insist on getting a kill during that time.

Fiora.build: To prepare for the physical damage from Fiora Q Lunge and Fiora E Bladework, start with Cloth Armor to build armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. If Fiora P Duelist's Dance and Fiora R Grand Challenge heal back your poke damage, fit in Executioner's Calling after you have built resistances.
Fiora.combo: In cannon form, poke by quickly chaining Jayce E Acceleration Gate and Jayce Q Shock Blast. If Fiora W Riposte is down and an opening to go in appears, hit her with cannon Q, then switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer and use Jayce Q To the Skies! → basic attack → Jayce W Lightning Field → Jayce E Thundering Blow in that order.
Fiora.escape: Right after Fiora uses Q Lunge is your chance to approach her. If Fiora W Riposte is also down, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, knock her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow, and trade briefly.
Fiora.fight: Stand opposite the vital marked by Fiora to limit her approach angle, and briefly counterattack right after Fiora Q Lunge. Use Jayce E Thundering Blow after Fiora W Riposte is down, and move sideways to account for Riposte.
Fiora.laning: In cannon form, poke Fiora as she goes for last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast while keeping the wave near the center. If Fiora closes in, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer to gain armor and push her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow; don't chase recklessly.
Fiora.phase: Jayce is strong early when he can use both forms, so build a lane advantage and turn it into objective gains in mid game.
Fiora.teamfight: Start the team fight from the back line with Jayce Q Shock Blast. If Fiora uses R Grand Challenge on Jayce, stand against a wall to cover one vital. Go in briefly with hammer only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to cannon and retreat.
Fiora.watch: Fiora W Riposte can negate attacks and stun you if it blocks the knockback from Jayce E Thundering Blow, so save E while Riposte is available. Watch when Fiora Q Lunge approaches from the direction of a vital on your body. If Fiora R Grand Challenge hits you, stand against a wall to cover one of your vitals.

Gangplank.build: Gangplank Q Parrrley and Gangplank E Powder Keg deal most of his damage as physical, so start with Cloth Armor, build armor first, and buy Plated Steelcaps. If Gangplank W Remove Scurvy heals back your poke damage, slot in Executioner's Calling. Resistance cannot block the true damage from Gangplank P Trial by Fire and Gangplank R Cannon Barrage.
Gangplank.combo: To poke, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. To engage, hit with Cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, then jump in with Jayce Q To the Skies! and use an auto attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow, in that order. If Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is still available, use Jayce E Thundering Blow after it is down, and account for the knockback direction.
Gangplank.escape: Engage just after Gangplank E Powder Keg is placed, while the barrel is not yet primed. Back off if there is a primed barrel nearby. After Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down, close the distance with Jayce Q To the Skies! and knock him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow. Gangplank has no ability to create distance on his own, so close in quickly when you get an opening.
Gangplank.fight: Trade when Gangplank E Powder Keg has just been placed and is not primed yet. Poke first with Jayce Q Shock Blast through Jayce E Acceleration Gate, then switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer and engage with Jayce Q To the Skies! when you see an opening. Using Jayce E Thundering Blow after Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down reduces the chance that your knockback will be cleansed.
Gangplank.laning: Poke with Jayce Q Shock Blast in Cannon form, keep the wave near the center, and disrupt Gangplank’s last hits. Jayce Q Shock Blast explodes on the first minion it hits, so fire when Gangplank behind the wave is within the blast radius. Back off if Gangplank E Powder Keg is primed nearby, and clear minions with Hammer auto attacks when mana is low.
Gangplank.phase: In the late game, Jayce is in danger if caught, so attack briefly and retreat.
Gangplank.teamfight: Start teamfights from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast through Jayce E Acceleration Gate. Avoid primed Gangplank E Powder Keg barrels and spots where barrels overlap, and make a brief Hammer engage only when the enemy formation is disrupted. After your combo, switch to Jayce R Mercury Cannon, land one auto attack, and retreat.
Gangplank.watch: Gangplank E Powder Keg slows when it explodes, so destroy the barrel from outside its blast radius before it becomes primed. Avoid primed barrels and spots where two barrels overlap.

Garen.build: Start with Cloth Armor to survive the early game, then buy Plated Steelcaps. Garen Q Decisive Strike and Garen E Judgment deal most of his damage as physical, so build armor first. If Garen P Perseverance heals back your poke damage, slot in Executioner's Calling.
Garen.combo: For basic poke, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate in Cannon form and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. To close in and finish, hit with Cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast, switch from Jayce R Mercury Cannon to Mercury Hammer, then use Jayce Q To the Skies!, an auto attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow, in that order. If Garen W Courage has just been used, delay Jayce E Thundering Blow by half a beat and plan your escape direction around the knockback.
Garen.escape: Garen has no mobility, so engage when Garen Q Decisive Strike is used on a minion or its empowered auto attack is down. Close the distance with Jayce Q To the Skies! and use Jayce E Thundering Blow with Garen’s escape direction in mind. Do not engage while Garen Q Decisive Strike is active, since you could be silenced.
Garen.fight: Keep your distance and poke briefly in Cannon form. Start a trade right after Garen Q Decisive Strike’s empowered auto attack is consumed. When Garen W Courage activates, wait half a beat instead of dumping your damage and Jayce E Thundering Blow. Do not fight for long inside Garen E Judgment; knock him away with Jayce E Thundering Blow and retreat.
Garen.laning: Early on, keep the wave near the center and harass with Cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast to disrupt Garen’s last hits. Pressure him so he has no time to build Garen W Courage’s permanent stacks. After pushing out the lane, use Garen’s difficulty impacting other lanes to create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
Garen.phase: Turn your early and mid-game lead into objectives. Garen’s Garen W Courage stacks are permanent, making him stronger over time, and Jayce is easy to catch in late-game teamfights, so pressure Garen’s scaling from the start.
Garen.teamfight: Start teamfights from the back with Cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast, and only make a brief engage when the enemy formation is disrupted. Do not enter range if Garen Q Decisive Strike is active or your health is low enough for Garen R Demacian Justice to kill you. After a Hammer combo, switch to Cannon and retreat immediately.
Garen.watch: Garen Q Decisive Strike empowers his next auto attack and silences, so do not engage first while it is active. When Garen E Judgment starts, knock him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow and move out of its range. Garen W Courage grants a shield and tenacity, so delay your combo by half a beat after he uses it. If your health is below half, stay outside the range of Garen R Demacian Justice, which resistance cannot block.

Gnar.build: Start with Cloth Armor, then buy Plated Steelcaps. Gnar’s main damage is physical, so build armor first, but remember that armor does not block the magic damage from Gnar W Hyper / Wallop.
Gnar.combo: In Cannon form, cast Jayce Q Shock Blast through Jayce E Acceleration Gate right after placing the gate. When you get a chance to engage, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, jump in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, then use an auto attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow, in that order.
Gnar.escape: The moment after Gnar uses Gnar E Hop / Crunch is your opening to engage. Close the distance with Jayce Q To the Skies! and knock him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow. If Gnar has just returned from Mega to Mini, engage while he cannot transform again.
Gnar.fight: Watch Gnar’s Rage and back off to wait out Mega Gnar right after he transforms. Look for a short trade with Jayce Q To the Skies! right after Gnar returns from Mega to Mini, or when Gnar E Hop / Crunch is down.
Gnar.laning: Early on, use Jayce Q Shock Blast in Cannon form to harass Mini Gnar when he goes for last hits. Keep the wave near the center, and avoid Gnar Q Boomerang Throw’s path so Gnar cannot catch it.
Gnar.phase: Jayce is strongest early, when he can use both forms, so turn your lane advantage into an objective lead. In late-game teamfights, you struggle to survive if caught, so poke from the back and make only brief engages.
Gnar.teamfight: Avoid standing with your back to a wall or in narrow terrain to deny Gnar R GNAR! a stun angle. Start fights from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast. If the enemy formation is disrupted right after Gnar returns from Mega to Mini, make a brief engage, then switch to Jayce R Mercury Cannon and retreat.
Gnar.watch: Gnar Q Boomerang Throw / Boulder Toss boomerangs can hit on the return, so move out of their path and move to prevent Gnar from catching them. Mega Gnar R GNAR! stuns when it knocks you into a wall, so avoid positioning with your back to one.

Gwen.build: Gwen deals mostly magic damage, and Jayce has relatively low magic resistance, so start with Null-Magic Mantle and buy Mercury's Treads. If Gwen P A Thousand Cuts heals back your poke damage, slot in Executioner's Calling. Gwen Q Snip Snip!’s center deals true damage that resistance cannot block, so manage your distance and angle along with your item choices.
Gwen.combo: After Gwen E Skip 'n Slash is down and Gwen W Hallowed Mist ends, hit with Cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast and switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer. Then close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, land the bonus magic damage from your first auto attack, use Jayce W Lightning Field, and knock her back with Jayce E Thundering Blow. Aim the knockback toward your allies or a wall so the chase is not interrupted.
Gwen.escape: Your opening to engage is right after Gwen uses her mobility tool, Gwen E Skip 'n Slash. Close the distance with Jayce Q To the Skies! and follow with Jayce E Thundering Blow so Gwen cannot get away. If Gwen W Hallowed Mist is active, wait for it to end before engaging.
Gwen.fight: Keep far enough away that Gwen cannot auto attack you and continue poking in Cannon form. Trade early, before Gwen Q Snip Snip! builds stacks, and avoid melee fights if she has full stacks. Look for a chance to close in with Jayce Q To the Skies! right after Gwen uses Gwen E Skip 'n Slash.
Gwen.laning: Use Cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast to disrupt Gwen’s last hits, but keep the wave near the center. When firing Jayce Q Shock Blast through Jayce E Acceleration Gate, keep the delay between placing the gate and firing short to give Gwen less time to dodge. If Gwen closes in, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer for the armor and knock her back with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Gwen.phase: In the early and mid game, turn that lead into an objective advantage. In late-game teamfights, Jayce is vulnerable if caught, so start with Cannon poke and keep engages brief.
Gwen.teamfight: Start teamfights from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast and keep your distance to avoid the area slow and maximum-health-based damage from Gwen R Needlework. Only make a brief Hammer combo engage when Gwen W Hallowed Mist has ended and the enemy formation is disrupted. Then switch to Cannon and retreat immediately.
Gwen.watch: Gwen Q Snip Snip! deals true damage in the center, which resistance cannot block, so move sideways when she closes in to avoid the center. When Gwen W Hallowed Mist is active, she cannot be targeted from outside the mist, so keep your distance until it ends. Gwen R Needlework slows in an area and deals damage based on maximum health, so maintain your distance in teamfights too.

Illaoi.build: Illaoi deals mostly physical damage and Jayce has low armor, so start with Cloth Armor, build armor first, and buy Plated Steelcaps. Slot in Executioner's Calling so Illaoi P Prophet of an Elder God’s healing does not undo your poke between trades. Illaoi W Harsh Lesson deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid building heavily into health alone.
Illaoi.combo: In Cannon form, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. If you dodge Illaoi E Test of Spirit and Illaoi W Harsh Lesson is down, and you can engage to finish, hit with Cannon Q, then switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer → Jayce Q To the Skies! → auto attack → Jayce W Lightning Field → Jayce E Thundering Blow, in that order. Do not skip the first auto attack after switching to Hammer.
Illaoi.escape: Illaoi W Harsh Lesson is her way to close distance, so if you have also dodged Illaoi E Test of Spirit right after she uses W, look for a chance to close the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies!. When you need to retreat, knock Illaoi away with Jayce E Thundering Blow, then create distance using the movement speed from switching weapons or Jayce E Acceleration Gate.
Illaoi.fight: Your opening to engage is after you dodge Illaoi E Test of Spirit and bait out Illaoi W Harsh Lesson. Poke first in Cannon form with Jayce Q Shock Blast through Jayce E Acceleration Gate, then switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer and engage with Jayce Q To the Skies!. Do not fight near tentacles while Illaoi R Leap of Faith is active.
Illaoi.laning: Do not fully push the wave; keep it near the center and away from walls to make it harder for Illaoi to fight near tentacles. Poke in Cannon form with Jayce Q Shock Blast and last-hit outside Illaoi E Test of Spirit’s range. If Illaoi engages, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer for the armor and knock her back with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Illaoi.phase: In the mid game, continue avoiding areas with tentacles and only take brief trades when Illaoi E Test of Spirit and Illaoi W Harsh Lesson are down. In late-game teamfights, Jayce struggles to survive if caught, so poke from the back and make only brief engages.
Illaoi.teamfight: Destroy tentacles when you can; otherwise, draw Illaoi into open ground away from walls. Illaoi R Leap of Faith creates one tentacle for each enemy champion it damages, so do not group up and spread out for its duration. Start teamfights from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast, and only make a brief Hammer engage when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to Cannon and retreat.
Illaoi.watch: Move outside the range of Illaoi E Test of Spirit to avoid having your spirit pulled out and being slowed and marked. If you can fight after your spirit is pulled out, retaliate; otherwise, break the tether and dodge the first tentacle. When Illaoi R Leap of Faith is active, do not fight near tentacles; spread out and wait out its duration.

Irelia.build: Start with Cloth Armor, then buy Plated Steelcaps. Irelia deals mostly physical damage and Jayce has low armor, so build armor first. If Irelia Q Bladesurge’s healing lets her sustain through your poke, slot in Executioner's Calling.
Irelia.combo: In Cannon form, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through the gate. If it hits, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, then use an auto attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow, in that order. When you need to push Irelia away, account for the knockback direction of Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Irelia.escape: The moment after Irelia uses Irelia Q Bladesurge is your opening to close the distance. If you have also dodged Irelia E Flawless Duet, engage with Jayce Q To the Skies! and follow up with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Irelia.fight: Look to trade and engage right after Irelia Q Bladesurge is down. Poke first in Cannon form with Jayce E Acceleration Gate and Jayce Q Shock Blast. If you get close, switch to Hammer and knock her back with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Irelia.laning: Do not leave low-health minions between you and Irelia, reducing her Irelia Q Bladesurge engage paths. Poke in Cannon form with Jayce Q Shock Blast, but if Irelia closes in, switch to Hammer and fight back.
Irelia.phase: In the mid game, turn that lead into denying her farm and taking objectives. In late-game teamfights, Jayce is vulnerable if caught, so poke from the back and make brief engages.
Irelia.teamfight: Start teamfights from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast and prioritize Irelia as a target. Irelia R Vanguard's Edge and Irelia E Flawless Duet can disrupt a teamfight, so only make a brief Hammer engage when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to Cannon and retreat.
Irelia.watch: Irelia Q Bladesurge can dash repeatedly through low-health minions, so create distance as minions are about to die. Dodge the stun from Irelia E Flawless Duet, and if you are trapped inside Irelia R Vanguard's Edge, wait until the blades disappear.

Jax.build: Jax relies on basic attacks and attack speed for damage, so prioritize considering items that reduce attack speed. Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so do not focus on just one type of resistance. Jax E Counter Strike deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid building heavily into health alone.
Jax.combo: Poke in Cannon form with a short delay between Jayce E Acceleration Gate and Jayce Q Shock Blast. If Jax E Counter Strike has ended and Jax Q Leap Strike is down, hit with Cannon Q, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, and close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!. Then use an auto attack right after switching, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow, in that order, and retreat.
Jax.escape: Your chance to close the distance is right after Jax uses Jax Q Leap Strike. However, if Jax E Counter Strike is active, move outside its stun range and wait until Counter Strike ends before engaging with Jayce Q To the Skies!. After engaging, knock Jax back with Jayce E Thundering Blow and end the trade quickly.
Jax.fight: Poke briefly in Cannon form, and do not stay in a long fight that lets Jax P Relentless Assault build attack speed. While Jax E Counter Strike is active, respond with abilities such as Jayce Q Shock Blast instead of auto attacks, and move outside its stun range. Engage briefly after Jax E Counter Strike ends and Jax Q Leap Strike is down.
Jax.laning: Keep the wave near the center and stay away from groups of minions that Jax can use as platforms for Jax Q Leap Strike. If Jax closes in, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, knock him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow, and avoid a prolonged fight.
Jax.phase: In the late game, Jayce is in danger if caught, so poke from the back and make brief engages before retreating.
Jax.teamfight: Poke from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast through Jayce E Acceleration Gate. If Jax activates Jax E Counter Strike and engages, do not group up nearby; move outside its stun range and wait out its duration. After the stun ends, push Jax away with Jayce E Thundering Blow, and only make a brief engage when the enemy formation is disrupted.
Jax.watch: When Jax E Counter Strike is active, stop auto attacking and move outside its stun range. Jax Q Leap Strike can use a minion or ward as a platform, so do not stand close to a group of minions. Do not use Jayce Q To the Skies! just because Jax activated Jax E Counter Strike; wait to see if he actually jumps in.

Kayle.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Kayle deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If Kayle W Celestial Blessing heals back the damage from your poke, fit in Executioner's Calling.
Kayle.combo: In Cannon form, cast Jayce E Acceleration Gate and fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it right away. If it hits, switch with Jayce R Mercury Hammer, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, then use a basic attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow in that order. Jayce E Thundering Blow knocks Kayle back, so account for the direction that will let you continue the chase.
Kayle.escape: Kayle has no mobility ability, so avoiding the slow from Kayle Q Radiant Blast creates an opening to engage. Kayle W Celestial Blessing can grant her movement speed, so close the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies! and choose the direction for Jayce E Thundering Blow to knock her back. After Kayle R Divine Judgment has been used, you can fight without worrying about damage immunity.
Kayle.fight: In Cannon form, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it to poke.
Kayle.laning: Keep the lane near the center and disrupt Kayle's last hits to build a CS and XP lead. In Cannon form, poke with Jayce Q Shock Blast, but when it explodes on a minion, check whether Kayle is in the blast radius. Kayle is vulnerable to ambushes, so call your jungler to approach from out of vision.
Kayle.teamfight: Start the fight from behind with Jayce Q Shock Blast and look for a flank or a route out of vision that reaches Kayle directly. Engage briefly when your allies' crowd control lands too, but if Kayle R Divine Judgment activates, knock her back with Jayce E Thundering Blow and let the invulnerability run out. After your Hammer combo, switch to Cannon immediately and disengage.
Kayle.watch: Kayle Q Radiant Blast slows and reduces armor and magic resistance, so avoid taking it head-on. Kayle E Starfire Spellblade deals damage based on missing health, so don't let trades drag on when your health is low. When Kayle R Divine Judgment is active, don't unload your damage. Use Jayce E Thundering Blow to knock her back and wait for the invulnerability to end.

Kennen.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first early on, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Kennen deals mostly magic damage, and Jayce has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Kennen.combo: In Cannon form, cast Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it to hit Kennen. If Kennen E Lightning Rush is down, switch with Jayce R Mercury Hammer, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, then use a basic attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow in that order. Your first basic attack after switching to Hammer deals bonus magic damage, so attack immediately.
Kennen.fight: In Cannon form, poke with Jayce E Acceleration Gate and Jayce Q Shock Blast to make Kennen use Kennen E Lightning Rush. Once Kennen E Lightning Rush is down, close the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies! and take a short trade. Account for the knockback direction when using Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Kennen.laning: Stand behind minions to block Kennen Q Thundering Shuriken, and expose yourself briefly only to last-hit. Keep the lane near the center and poke with Jayce Q Shock Blast in Cannon form to disrupt Kennen's last hits. Back off briefly when Kennen P Mark of the Storm has marked you twice.
Kennen.phase: Jayce is strongest early, when he can use both forms, so build a lane advantage and extend it with midgame objectives. In late-game team fights, Jayce is vulnerable if caught, so poke first with Jayce Q Shock Blast and keep engages short.
Kennen.teamfight: Spread out from your allies to avoid a multi-person stun from Kennen R Slicing Maelstrom, and use vision to cover the spots where Kennen could engage. Start the team fight from behind with Jayce Q Shock Blast, and go in briefly with Hammer only when the enemy formation is disrupted. Don't stay where you engaged; switch to Jayce R Mercury Cannon and disengage.
Kennen.watch: You are stunned when Kennen P Mark of the Storm reaches three stacks, so back off when you have two marks and wait for them to expire. Dodge Kennen Q Thundering Shuriken from behind minions, and don't stand grouped with allies in your approach path where Kennen R Slicing Maelstrom can stun multiple targets.
Kennen.escape: Kennen E Lightning Rush being down is Jayce’s window to engage. If Kennen P Mark of the Storm has stacked twice on you, back off and wait for the stacks to disappear before going in.

Kled.build: Buy Cloth Armor early to survive, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Kled's main damage is physical, and Jayce has low armor, so build armor first. Kled W Violent Tendencies and Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! deal damage based on maximum health, so be wary of choices that only add a lot of health.
Kled.combo: To poke, cast Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. When you have a chance to finish him, hit with Jayce Q Shock Blast in Cannon form, switch with Jayce R Mercury Hammer, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, then use a basic attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow in that order. Use the final knockback based on the direction that lets you continue the chase.
Kled.escape: If only Kled E Jousting is down, Kled can still escape with Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!!, so don't engage hastily. Look especially for an opening before Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! comes back, close the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies!, and use Jayce E Thundering Blow. If Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope catches you, focus first on getting out before it pulls you in.
Kled.fight: In Cannon form, poke first with Jayce E Acceleration Gate and Jayce Q Shock Blast. If Kled W Violent Tendencies is active, create distance to avoid his fourth attack, then fight again. If Kled gets close, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer to hold your ground and knock him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Kled.laning: Keep the lane near the center and disrupt Kled's last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast in Cannon form. Kled regains Skaarl by building courage after being dismounted, so create distance if you can't finish him for certain. After dismounting him, push him away from the wave so he can't build courage by killing minions.
Kled.phase: Jayce is strong early, when he can use both forms, so build a lane advantage and extend it with objectives. Kled weakens after lane and midgame, so you gain an advantage if you avoid giving him an early lead. In late game, Jayce is also at risk if caught, so don't stay where you engage.
Kled.teamfight: Watch for Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! with flank vision, and don't break formation if you have a tank in front. Start the fight from behind with Jayce Q Shock Blast in Cannon form, and go in briefly only when the enemy formation is disrupted. After your Hammer combo, switch to Cannon immediately and disengage.
Kled.watch: If you are caught by Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope, create distance before it pulls you in. When Kled W Violent Tendencies is ready, its fourth attack deals dangerous damage based on your maximum health, so don't fight within range of four consecutive attacks. Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! can engage from far away outside vision, so watch your flanks.

KSante.build: Start with Cloth Armor to survive the early game, then buy Plated Steelcaps. K'Sante deals mostly physical damage and Jayce has low armor, so build armor first. If K'Sante’s crowd control often starts fights and leaves you locked down, fit Quicksilver Sash between core items.
KSante.combo: In Cannon form, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it to poke. To engage, hit with Cannon Q, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, then use an auto attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow, in that order. Aim Hammer E carefully so you do not accidentally knock K'Sante outside Jayce’s range.
KSante.escape: Do not engage just because only one of K'Sante W Path Maker and K'Sante E Footwork is down. Watch both mobility tools and K'Sante Q Ntofo Strikes’ pull, and especially look for an opening before K'Sante R All Out comes back up. Then close the distance with Jayce Q To the Skies! and use Jayce E Thundering Blow to stop K'Sante from escaping.
KSante.fight: When K'Sante W Path Maker is charging, hold your damage and Jayce E Thundering Blow, and dodge to the side. When K'Sante R All Out activates, focus your damage on his reduced health and resistances, but do not try to handle K'Sante alone while his damage and lifesteal are stronger. If he closes in, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer for the armor and use Jayce E Thundering Blow to control the distance.
KSante.laning: Keep the wave near the center and aim Cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast at where K'Sante will move or at a spot near minions where the blast will reach him. Watch K'Sante Q Ntofo Strikes’ stacks and create distance when his next pulling Q is ready.
KSante.phase: In the mid game, turn your lead into objectives and widen it before K'Sante stacks defensive items. Jayce is vulnerable if caught in late-game teamfights, so poke from the back and make brief engages.
KSante.teamfight: Start the fight from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast through Jayce E Acceleration Gate, and make a brief Hammer engage only when K'Sante’s formation is disrupted. Focus damage on K'Sante with your team while K'Sante R All Out is active, but do not let K'Sante keep hitting multiple people. If the fight will be prolonged, make sure at least one teammate has a source of healing reduction. After a Hammer combo, switch to Jayce R Mercury Cannon and retreat while landing an auto attack to reduce resistances.
KSante.watch: If you are hit by K'Sante Q Ntofo Strikes repeatedly or K'Sante builds stacks by hitting minions, watch for the next Q’s pull and stun, and move outside its range. When K'Sante W Path Maker is charged, do not use Jayce E Thundering Blow; dodge to the side of its charge direction. Do not face off with your back to a wall where K'Sante R All Out can knock you through it.

Malphite.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first early on, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Malphite's main damage—Q Seismic Shard, E Ground Slam, and R Unstoppable Force—is magic damage, so build magic resistance first.
Malphite.combo: Poke first to break Malphite P Granite Shield, then in Cannon form cast Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. When engaging, use this order: hit with Jayce Q Shock Blast → switch with Jayce R Mercury Hammer → leap with Jayce Q To the Skies! → basic attack → Jayce W Lightning Field → Jayce E Thundering Blow. Choose the final knockback based on the direction that lets you continue the chase.
Malphite.escape: When Malphite R Unstoppable Force is down, you have an opening to engage.
Malphite.fight: Break Malphite P Granite Shield first, then poke at short intervals to damage his actual health. Avoid trading right after Malphite Q Seismic Shard hits. When Malphite R Unstoppable Force is down, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies! and follow up with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Malphite.laning: Disrupt last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast in Cannon form, but don't push the lane all the way; keep it near the center. Malphite Q Seismic Shard can't be dodged from behind minions, so don't stay within range for long.
Malphite.phase: In late game, Jayce is vulnerable if caught, so attack briefly and disengage.
Malphite.teamfight: Spread out from your allies so Malphite R Unstoppable Force doesn't knock up multiple people. Poke from behind with Jayce Q Shock Blast fired through Jayce E Acceleration Gate, then counterattack as soon as Malphite R Unstoppable Force is down. Go in briefly with Hammer only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to Cannon and disengage.
Malphite.watch: Malphite Q Seismic Shard slows you, making trades and retreating difficult, so don't start a fight right after it hits. Malphite R Unstoppable Force is an unstoppable dash that Jayce E Thundering Blow cannot interrupt. When Malphite is out of sight, don't give him an angle to engage near walls or bushes.

Mordekaiser.build: Mordekaiser deals mostly magic damage, and Jayce has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Buy a Null-Magic Mantle early, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Mordekaiser W Indestructible converts its remaining shield into health, so fit in Executioner's Calling.
Mordekaiser.combo: To poke, cast Jayce E Acceleration Gate in Cannon form and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. If Mordekaiser E Death's Grasp misses and you have an opening to engage, hit with Cannon Q, then switch with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, and use a basic attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow in that order. If Mordekaiser W Indestructible has just granted a shield, delay when you focus your damage.
Mordekaiser.escape: When Mordekaiser E Death's Grasp misses, you have an opening to go in. Mordekaiser has no ability to create distance, so you can close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, but don't enter Mordekaiser R Realm of Death range alone if it's ready. End the trade by knocking him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow, then create distance before Mordekaiser P Darkness Rise activates.
Mordekaiser.fight: In Cannon form, cast Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it for a short poke. Back off before Mordekaiser P Darkness Rise activates, and don't unload your damage right after Mordekaiser W Indestructible grants a shield. Engage after Mordekaiser E Death's Grasp misses, but don't duel alone within range of Mordekaiser R Realm of Death.
Mordekaiser.laning: Early on, poke in Cannon form with Jayce Q Shock Blast to disrupt Mordekaiser's last hits. Don't push the lane all the way; keep it near the center. Keep your distance to avoid Mordekaiser E Death's Grasp, and if he gets close, switch to Hammer and knock him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Mordekaiser.phase: In midgame, turn that advantage into objectives and a lead. In late-game team fights, Jayce is vulnerable if caught, so fight from a position where Mordekaiser can't trap you.
Mordekaiser.teamfight: Start the fight from behind with Jayce Q Shock Blast, and spread out from your allies so Mordekaiser E Death's Grasp doesn't pull in several of you at once. Mordekaiser has low mobility, so use Jayce's slow and Jayce E Thundering Blow to keep your distance. Go in briefly only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to Cannon and disengage; don't stay alone within Mordekaiser R Realm of Death range.
Mordekaiser.watch: If Mordekaiser E Death's Grasp pulls you in, it can be followed by Mordekaiser Q Obliterate and Mordekaiser P Darkness Rise, so keep your distance when facing him. Mordekaiser P Darkness Rise activates after three hits from abilities or basic attacks, so trade briefly and back off. When Mordekaiser R Realm of Death is ready, don't enter its range alone and get trapped in a duel without your allies' help.

Nasus.build: Nasus's main damage, Nasus Q Siphoning Strike, is physical, so start with Cloth Armor and build armor first. Choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Armor can't block the magic damage from Nasus E Spirit Fire and Nasus R Fury of the Sands, so leave the ground effect and keep your distance while R is active.
Nasus.combo: In Cannon form, cast Jayce E Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate and immediately hit with Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast through it. When an opportunity to close in appears, switch to Hammer with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer, leap in with Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast, then immediately use a basic attack and Jayce W Lightning Field. Aim the final Jayce E Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate to knock Nasus toward an ally or a wall.
Nasus.escape: After Nasus W Wither is down, you have an opening to close the gap. Nasus has no escape tool besides Flash, so if Flash is down too, leap in with Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast in Hammer form. Don't go in without a clear advantage while Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active.
Nasus.fight: Early on, poke with Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast in Cannon form when Nasus goes for a last hit with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. Cast Jayce E Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Q through the gate to increase the poke's range, speed, and damage. Look to engage when Nasus W Wither is down and Nasus R Fury of the Sands is inactive.
Nasus.laning: Don't push the lane all the way to Nasus's turret; keep it near the center to disrupt last hits with Nasus Q Siphoning Strike. If the lane pushes toward your side, call your jungler to pressure Nasus, who has no escape tool besides Flash.
Nasus.phase: Carry your early and midgame lane advantage into objectives. As Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks up, the matchup gets worse over time, so don't fight head-on for long in late game.
Nasus.teamfight: Start the fight from behind with Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast and attack Nasus while keeping your distance. Don't fight him while Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active unless you have a clear advantage. Go in briefly with Hammer only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to Cannon with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer and disengage.
Nasus.watch: Nasus W Wither reduces your movement and attack speed, so don't face him alone while affected; create distance. Nasus grows stronger when Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active, so unless you have a clear advantage, avoid fighting and let its duration run out. Nasus E Spirit Fire reduces armor, so don't stay on the ground effect.

Olaf.build: Buy Cloth Armor first early on, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Olaf's main damage is physical, so build armor first, while accounting for the fact that armor does not work against Olaf E Reckless Swing.
Olaf.combo: To poke, cast Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. To engage, hit with Cannon Q, switch with Jayce R Mercury Hammer, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, then use a basic attack → Jayce W Lightning Field → Jayce E Thundering Blow in that order. If Olaf R Ragnarok is active, delay any engage that relies on E's knockback.
Olaf.escape: Olaf has no ability to create distance, so you have an opening to engage when he can't retrieve Olaf Q Undertow's axe and Olaf R Ragnarok has ended. Close the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies! and fight while choosing the knockback direction for Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Olaf.fight: Poke with Jayce Q Shock Blast in Cannon form and avoid fights where Olaf can get close. Prevent Olaf from retrieving the axe from Olaf Q Undertow, and attack briefly when an opportunity to close the gap appears after Olaf R Ragnarok ends.
Olaf.laning: Keep the lane near the center and use your range advantage in Cannon form to disrupt Olaf's last hits. Move opposite the side where Olaf Q Undertow's axe lands to make it harder for him to approach again. If Olaf catches you, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer to gain armor, and if Olaf R Ragnarok is inactive, knock him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Olaf.phase: Both champions are strong early, and this is also Olaf's peak, so focus on avoiding deaths. Jayce needs to build a lead through poke and lane advantage in the early and midgame. Olaf becomes relatively weaker late, but Jayce is also at risk if caught, so keep your distance.
Olaf.teamfight: Start the team fight from behind with Jayce Q Shock Blast fired through Jayce E Acceleration Gate. If Olaf R Ragnarok is active, create distance and let it run out. Go in briefly with Hammer only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to Cannon and disengage.
Olaf.watch: Olaf Q Undertow slows and reduces armor, so dodge the axe's path and move to the opposite side of where it lands to prevent him from retrieving it. When Olaf R Ragnarok is active, don't rely on Jayce E Thundering Blow to knock him back; create distance. Olaf E Reckless Swing deals true damage that armor can't reduce, so avoid getting close when your health is low.

Ornn.combo: In Cannon form, hit first with Jayce E Acceleration Gate and Jayce Q Shock Blast. To engage, switch to Hammer with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer, close in with Jayce Q To the Skies!, then use a basic attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, and Jayce E Thundering Blow in that order. Use Jayce E Thundering Blow to knock Ornn in a direction you can chase, or to knock him away and end the trade.
Ornn.escape: Look to engage after both Ornn E Searing Charge and Ornn R Call of the Forge God are down. In particular, close the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies! and use Jayce E Thundering Blow before Ornn R Call of the Forge God comes back.
Ornn.fight: In Cannon form, cast Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it to poke. Even if Ornn E Searing Charge is down, don't rush in while Ornn R Call of the Forge God is still available. If Ornn gets close, switch to Hammer, fight back, and end the trade by knocking him away with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Ornn.laning: Early on, disrupt Ornn's last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast in Cannon form while keeping the lane near the center. If Ornn tries to forge an item in lane, approach and attack to interrupt him. Avoid the area around Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture's pillar, and don't let Ornn E Searing Charge hit you while your back is to a wall.
Ornn.phase: Early on, Jayce can use both forms and Ornn's damage is low, so build a lane advantage. In midgame, turn it into an objective lead and pressure Ornn before his items and his allies' Masterwork upgrades stack up. In late-game team fights, Jayce is vulnerable if caught, so attack briefly and disengage.
Ornn.teamfight: Start the team fight from behind with Jayce Q Shock Blast fired through Jayce E Acceleration Gate. Avoid the line between the spirit and Ornn for Ornn R Call of the Forge God, and go in briefly with Hammer only when the enemy formation is disrupted. After your combo, switch to Cannon with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer and disengage.
Ornn.watch: Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture's pillar becomes a wall that knocks you airborne when Ornn E Searing Charge collides with it, so move away from pillars and terrain walls toward open ground. If the final flame of Ornn W Bellows Breath makes you Brittle, keep your distance until the effect ends to avoid the bonus damage and long crowd control. Move out of the line between the spirit and Ornn for Ornn R Call of the Forge God, and watch the path where the spirit turns back after passing.

Pantheon.build: Start with Cloth Armor to survive lane, and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Pantheon's main damage is physical and Jayce has low armor, so build armor first.
Pantheon.combo: After Pantheon E Aegis Assault ends, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. If Pantheon W Shield Vault is down and you can get in, land cannon Q, switch forms with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer, then close in with Jayce Q To the Skies! and use a basic attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, then Jayce E Thundering Blow. Aim the final knockback in the direction you want to push Pantheon.
Pantheon.escape: Treat Pantheon W Shield Vault being down, when he can't use his stun and dash, as an opening to engage. If Pantheon R Grand Starfall is still on cooldown, close the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies! and fight while knocking him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow. If only one of Pantheon's mobility tools is down, he can still escape with the other, so don't chase too far.
Pantheon.fight: Poke with Jayce Q Shock Blast through Jayce E Acceleration Gate from outside Pantheon W Shield Vault range. Go in briefly after Pantheon E Aegis Assault ends and Pantheon W Shield Vault is down. If Pantheon engages first, switch to hammer form with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer to gain armor, then knock him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Pantheon.laning: Keep the lane near the center and disrupt Pantheon's last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form. Don't push the wave all the way in and let Pantheon farm comfortably.
Pantheon.phase: In mid game, turn your lane lead into objective control. Pantheon's impact falls off later, but Jayce is also vulnerable if caught in a late-game team fight, so keep your distance.
Pantheon.teamfight: Start fights from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast and stay out of Pantheon W Shield Vault range. If Pantheon E Aegis Assault faces you, wait for it to end or attack from the side. Go in briefly with hammer form only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to cannon and disengage.
Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault is a targeted stun, so stay out of its range. Pantheon E Aegis Assault blocks damage from the direction he faces, so don't attack from the front; wait for it to end or attack from the side. When you see the landing indicator for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, walk out of its landing area.

Poppy.build: In the early game, start with Cloth Armor to survive and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Poppy's main damage is physical, so build armor first.
Poppy.combo: To poke, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate in cannon form and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. When fighting after Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends, use cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast → switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer → Jayce Q To the Skies! → basic attack → Jayce W Lightning Field → Jayce E Thundering Blow. Jayce E Thundering Blow knocks Poppy back, so aim it carefully.
Poppy.escape: Right after you bait out Poppy E Heroic Charge, use the opening while her mobility tool is down to close the gap. If Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, wait for its duration to end before engaging with Jayce Q To the Skies!.
Poppy.fight: Right after Poppy uses Poppy E Heroic Charge and after Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends are opportunities to engage with Jayce Q To the Skies! Before going in, poke from cannon form with Jayce Q Shock Blast through Jayce E Acceleration Gate. If Poppy engages first, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer to fight back and knock her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Poppy.laning: Poke from outside Poppy’s range with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form and keep the lane near the center. Don't stand with a wall behind you to avoid the stun from Poppy E Heroic Charge, and step on the shield dropped by Poppy P Iron Ambassador first to deny her shield.
Poppy.phase: Turn that lead into objectives in the early to mid game. In late game, one catch can be dangerous, so fight briefly and disengage.
Poppy.teamfight: Start fights from the back with cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast. Go in briefly for a hammer combo only when the enemy formation is disrupted and Poppy W Steadfast Presence has ended. Immediately switch to Jayce R Mercury Cannon to disengage.
Poppy.watch: Poppy E Heroic Charge stuns if it hits a wall, so don't stand with a wall behind you; stay in open space. Don't leap in with Jayce Q To the Skies! while Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active. If you're hit by Poppy Q Hammer Shock, immediately walk out of the remaining zone. If you see Poppy charging Poppy R Keeper's Verdict, move to the side from in front of her.

Quinn.build: Start with Cloth Armor to survive lane, and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Quinn's damage is mostly physical and Jayce has relatively low armor, so build armor first.
Quinn.combo: After Quinn E Vault is down, land Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, then engage with Jayce Q To the Skies!. Follow with the empowered basic attack after switching, Jayce W Lightning Field, then Jayce E Thundering Blow. Aim the final knockback so you don't send Quinn outside your attack range.
Quinn.escape: Quinn E Vault is her escape tool, so its use creates an opening to engage. Don't force an engage before then; if you see it used, approach with Jayce Q To the Skies!.
Quinn.fight: When Quinn P Harrier is not marking you, poke with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form. If Quinn E Vault is down, close the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies! and fight while aiming hammer-form Jayce E Thundering Blow to knock Quinn back in the direction you want.
Quinn.laning: Keep the lane near the center, disrupt Quinn's last hits, and poke with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form. Stand behind the minion line to block Quinn Q Blinding Assault, and move outside basic attack range if Quinn P Harrier marks you. If Quinn engages, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer to gain armor, then fight back.
Quinn.phase: Jayce is strongest early, when he can use both forms, so build a lane lead. In mid game, turn that lead into objectives. In late-game team fights, Jayce is easy to catch, so poke from the back.
Quinn.teamfight: Start from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form. Go in briefly with hammer form only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then switch to cannon and disengage. If Quinn comes in from the side, knock her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Quinn.watch: If Quinn P Harrier marks you, her empowered basic attacks hurt, so move outside Quinn's basic attack range. Dodge Quinn Q Blinding Assault from behind minions, and don't throw skillshots while your vision is reduced. Quinn E Vault knocks Jayce away and marks him, so don't force an engage before it is down.

Renekton.build: Start with Cloth Armor to survive, and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Renekton's main damage is physical and Jayce has low armor, so build armor first. If Renekton heals back your poke damage with Renekton Q Cull the Meek, fit in Executioner's Calling.
Renekton.combo: First, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate in cannon form and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it to hit him. If Renekton's dash and stun are down and you can engage, use cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast → switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer → Jayce Q To the Skies! → basic attack → Jayce W Lightning Field → Jayce E Thundering Blow. Aim the final knockback in the direction you want to push him.
Renekton.escape: Right after Renekton uses Renekton E Slice and Dice to disengage is an opportunity to go in. If Renekton W Ruthless Predator is also down and he has no Fury, counterattack by closing the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies!. If those abilities are still available, hold off on engaging.
Renekton.fight: When Renekton has no Fury, poke with Jayce Q Shock Blast through Jayce E Acceleration Gate in cannon form. Fight back after Renekton has used Renekton Q Cull the Meek, Renekton W Ruthless Predator, and Renekton E Slice and Dice.
Renekton.laning: Keep the lane near the center and disrupt last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast from outside range in cannon form. Poke when Renekton walks forward to build Fury by hitting minions, but avoid positions where he can use the minions as stepping stones for his dashes. If Renekton engages, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer to gain armor and knock him away with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Renekton.phase: In the early to mid game, build a lead through lane and objectives without giving up kills. Renekton's value falls off from mid game onward, but Jayce is also vulnerable if caught in a late-game team fight, so keep your distance.
Renekton.teamfight: Start from the back with cannon Jayce Q Shock Blast and go in briefly only when the enemy formation is disrupted. After a hammer combo, switch straight back to cannon and disengage; don't stay where you engaged. On the retreat, use Jayce E Acceleration Gate to help your allies move too.
Renekton.watch: When Renekton P Reign of Anger puts his Fury above half, stay out of range to avoid the long stun from empowered Renekton W Ruthless Predator. Even just below half, he can build Fury with a basic attack or Renekton Q Cull the Meek, so don't let your guard down. Renekton E Slice and Dice unlocks a second dash if it hits a unit, so don't stand in or behind a minion wave.

Riven.build: Start with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Riven's main damage is physical, so build armor first; if Riven gets ahead, prioritize defensive items sooner. Riven R Blade of the Exile deals more damage based on your missing health, so consider building health too.
Riven.combo: To poke, place Jayce E Acceleration Gate and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it. If Riven Q Broken Wings is down and you can engage, land cannon-form Jayce Q Shock Blast, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, then close in with Jayce Q To the Skies! and use a basic attack, Jayce W Lightning Field, then Jayce E Thundering Blow. Don't miss the bonus magic damage on your first basic attack after switching to hammer, and aim Jayce E Thundering Blow carefully.
Riven.escape: Don't engage just because Riven E Valor is down. Close the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies! before Riven Q Broken Wings comes back, especially right after she uses it to clear minions. If Riven gets on you and starts a combo, knock her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow and disengage.
Riven.fight: When Riven uses Riven Q Broken Wings to clear minions, that's an opportunity to trade. Poke with Jayce E Acceleration Gate and Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form, and if Riven engages, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer to gain armor. Don't use Jayce E Thundering Blow before she engages; use it to knock her back as soon as she gets on you.
Riven.laning: Keep the lane near the center and disrupt Riven's last hits with Jayce Q Shock Blast from cannon form range. Don't push the wave all the way in; pressure her when Riven Q Broken Wings is used to clear minions. If you've pushed too far out of vision, watch out for Riven Q Broken Wings and Riven E Valor both being available.
Riven.phase: In the early to mid game, use the openings when Riven's mobility abilities are down to build a lane lead and an objective advantage. In late-game team fights, Jayce is vulnerable if caught, so keep your distance from the back.
Riven.teamfight: Start fights from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast and respond to Riven's engage by knocking her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow. Go in briefly for a hammer combo only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then immediately switch to Jayce R Mercury Cannon to disengage.
Riven.watch: Riven Q Broken Wings and Riven E Valor chain short dashes to cover a long distance, so move back when you see the first dash. If Riven gets on you, watch out for the knock-up from Riven Q Broken Wings and the stun from Riven W Ki Burst, and knock her away with Jayce E Thundering Blow. If Riven R Blade of the Exile is active, her range and attack damage increase, so create distance until its duration ends.

Rumble.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Rumble's main damage is magic, so choose defensive items with magic resistance.
Rumble.combo: After Rumble W Scrap Shield's shield is down, land Jayce Q Shock Blast, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, then engage with Jayce Q To the Skies!. Use a basic attack immediately after switching, then Jayce W Lightning Field, and knock him back with Jayce E Thundering Blow. Aim the knockback so you do not send Rumble outside your attack range and interrupt your combo.
Rumble.escape: If you're hit by the first shot of Rumble E Electro Harpoon, use the movement speed from Jayce P Hextech Capacitor or Jayce E Acceleration Gate to create distance before the second shot arrives. Look to engage after Rumble uses Rumble W Scrap Shield, once you've briefly waited out the shield. Rumble has no mobility ability, so after you get in, aim Jayce E Thundering Blow carefully.
Rumble.fight: Poke from outside Rumble Q Flamespitter range to reduce the time you're exposed to it, and make Rumble walk forward. If Rumble activates Rumble W Scrap Shield, don't dump burst damage into the shield; wait briefly. After Rumble uses Rumble W Scrap Shield, look for the opening while his escape tool is down and engage with Jayce Q To the Skies!.
Rumble.laning: Poke with Jayce Q Shock Blast in cannon form, keep the lane near the center, and disrupt Rumble's last hits. When placing Jayce E Acceleration Gate and firing Jayce Q Shock Blast, shorten the gap between the two abilities to give him less time to dodge. If Rumble engages, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer to gain resistances and knock him away with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Rumble.phase: Poke Rumble in the early to mid game to build a lane lead and an objective advantage. Jayce is vulnerable if caught in a late-game team fight, so don't stay in melee range for long.
Rumble.teamfight: Start fights from the back with Jayce Q Shock Blast and go in briefly only when the enemy formation is disrupted. After a hammer combo, immediately switch to Jayce R Mercury Cannon to disengage. If you're hit by the first shot of Rumble E Electro Harpoon, create distance before another harpoon catches you.
Rumble.watch: If you're hit by the first shot of Rumble E Electro Harpoon, immediately create distance before the second harpoon arrives. Getting hit in succession greatly increases the slow and reduces your magic resistance, making you take more damage from Rumble Q Flamespitter. Watch out for the slow from Rumble R The Equalizer.

Sett.build: Start with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Sett's damage is mostly physical and Jayce has low armor, so build armor first. Sett W Haymaker's center true damage can't be reduced by resistances, so dodge it by repositioning.
Sett.combo: Hit Sett with Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast in cannon form, switch with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer, then leap in with Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast. Follow with a basic attack right after switching, Jayce W Lightning Field / Hyper Charge, then the knockback from Jayce E Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate. Sett W Haymaker can get stronger, so create distance after the combo and avoid the center of its aiming line.
Sett.escape: If Sett E Facebreaker is also down, engage with Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast and use Jayce E Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate. If Sett still has crowd control available, stay out of range first.
Sett.fight: If Sett approaches with Sett Q Knuckle Down, switch to hammer form with Jayce R Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer to gain armor, then use Jayce E Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate to knock him back and create distance again. After dealing a large amount of damage, briefly back off in anticipation of Sett W Haymaker.
Sett.laning: Poke from outside Sett’s range in cannon form with Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast through Jayce E Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate. Keep the gap between the gate and Q short to give Sett less time to dodge. Keep the lane near the center and disrupt Sett's last hits, but avoid positions where Sett E Facebreaker can catch you and minions from both sides.
Sett.phase: In late game, Jayce is vulnerable if caught because of his low armor and health. The information provided isn't enough to determine when Sett gets stronger.
Sett.teamfight: Start fights from the back with Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast and watch out for positions where Sett R The Show Stopper can grab or throw you. Go in briefly for a hammer combo only when the enemy formation is disrupted, then immediately switch to cannon and disengage. When Sett W Haymaker comes out, sidestep the center of its aiming line.
Sett.watch: If Sett walks in with Sett Q Knuckle Down, create distance before he gains movement speed. Sett W Haymaker gets stronger after he takes damage, so briefly back off after attacking, and when he casts it, sidestep the center of the aiming line to avoid the true damage. If Sett E Facebreaker catches targets on both sides of Sett, it stuns you, so don't stand between Sett and a minion wave.

Shen.build: The time spent taunted by Shen E Shadow Dash is dangerous, so prioritize tenacity. Shen E Shadow Dash deals physical damage and Shen Q Twilight Assault deals magic damage, so don't focus on only one resistance if you build resistances. Shen Q Twilight Assault deals damage based on max health, so stacking health alone is less effective.
Shen.combo: Place Jayce E Acceleration Gate in cannon form and immediately fire Jayce Q Shock Blast through it to poke. When Shen E Shadow Dash misses and Shen W Spirit's Refuge can't block your basic attacks, land Jayce Q Shock Blast, switch to Jayce R Mercury Hammer, then close in with Jayce Q To the Skies! and trade with a basic attack → Jayce W Lightning Field → Jayce E Thundering Blow. Calculate in advance the direction to knock Shen back with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
Shen.escape: Right after Shen E Shadow Dash misses is Jayce's opening to engage. If Shen R Stand United is also down and hasn't come off cooldown, Shen has fewer opportunities to escape with a mobility ability, so close the gap with Jayce Q To the Skies! and knock him away with Jayce E Thundering Blow.
